spots.bio: Craft and design studios and galleries for glass, ceramics, furniture and jewellery, with tours.
spots.name: JamFactory
spots.note: SATC lists JamFactory's studios and galleries (ceramics, glass, furniture, jewellery) with workshop tours; visitors can see makers at work and free gallery shows. Case against: part shop and a not-for-profit studio.

spots.bio: State heritage cemetery with guided heritage tours.
spots.name: West Terrace Cemetery
spots.note: SATC lists Adelaide Cemetery Tours of this State heritage cemetery; the Adelaide Cemeteries Authority offers 7-day self-guided interpretive trails (about an hour) plus guided tours. Case against: cemetery; some visit by tour.

spots.bio: Small permanent museum with exhibits and education centre, booking needed on some days.
spots.wiki: Adelaide Holocaust Museum and Andrew Steiner Education Centre
spots.name: Adelaide Holocaust Museum
spots.note: Wikivoyage lists it with hours (Sun, Tue-Thu; booking on Tue-Thu), $10; a permanent small museum open to the public. Second-tier museum a guide names. Case against: limited days, bookings, single source.

spots.bio: Volunteer-run military museum at Keswick Barracks with guns, artillery and wartime displays.
spots.name: Army Museum of South Australia
spots.note: Wikivoyage lists the volunteer-run military museum (guns, artillery, WWI/WWII/Korea/Vietnam), $5; permanent museum a guide names. Case against: limited hours (Sun, Mon, Wed), one source.

spots.bio: Local history museum of Holdfast Bay in Glenelg Town Hall on Moseley Square.
spots.name: Bay Discovery Centre
spots.note: Wikivoyage names the local-history museum in Glenelg Town Hall on Moseley Square. Permanent small museum a guide names. Case against: one source.

spots.bio: Seafront amusement park at Glenelg with a carousel, bumper cars, mini-golf and a mini train.
spots.name: The Beachouse
spots.note: Wikivoyage lists this permanent seafront amusement park (mini-golf, carousel, bumper cars, mini train, slides); open daily. Against: a ticketed business.

spots.bio: Self-guided Kaurna heritage walk through the city with art and stories.
spots.name: Kaurna Trail
spots.note: Experience Adelaide (city tourism) lists the self-guided Kaurna heritage walk with art and stories; a permanent named route.

spots.bio: South Australia's first national park, with trails, an old government house and picnic areas.
spots.name: Belair National Park

spots.bio: Adelaide's newest national park at O'Halloran Hill, with trails over former farmland.
spots.name: Glenthorne National Park
spots.note: Wikivoyage names it as Adelaide's third national park and the parks agency has a page; a national park with walking trails and a visitor offer.

spots.bio: Gorge park with the Sturt tillite glacial rocks, grey box woodland and walking and bike trails.
spots.name: Sturt Gorge Recreation Park
spots.note: NPWS SA lists the park: Sturt tillite glacial rocks, grey box woodland, new mountain-bike and hiking trails on the Craigburn Farm addition, waterholes along the Sturt River.

spots.bio: Hills-edge park with walking and mountain-biking trails.
spots.name: Anstey Hill Recreation Park

spots.bio: Steep 3-4 hour climb past First and Second Falls to the Mount Lofty summit.
spots.name: Waterfall Gully to Mount Lofty Summit Track
spots.note: Distinct, popular 3-4 hr climb past First and Second Falls to the summit; agency Cleland National Park page names the walk, plus walking guides. Part-of-larger risk is small: Mount Lofty Summit and Waterfall Gully are separate spots, the track is its own walk.
